pairs: Simile est regnum cælorum homini patrifamilias, qui exiit primo mane conducere operarios in vineam suam.
“The kingdom of heaven is like the father of a family who went out in early morning to lead workers into his vineyard.
Conventione autem facta cum operariis ex denario diurno,
Then, having made an agreement with the workers for one denarius per day,
he sent them into his vineyard.
And going out about the third hour,
vidit alios stantes in foro otiosos,
he saw others standing idle in the marketplace.
et quod justum fuerit dabo vobis.
and what I will give you will be just.’
So they went forth. But again,
Iterum autem exiit circa sextam et nonam horam:
he went out about the sixth, and about the ninth hour,
Yet truly, about the eleventh hour,
he went out and found others standing,
Quid hic statis tota die otiosi?
‘Why have you stood here idle all day?’
Ite et vos in vineam meam.
‘You also may go into my vineyard.’
dicit dominus vineæ procuratori suo: Voca operarios,
the lord of the vineyard said to his manager,
et redde illis mercedem incipiens a novissimis usque ad primos.
‘Call the workers and pay them their wages, beginning from the last, even to the first.’
Cum venissent ergo qui circa undecimam horam venerant,
And so, when those who had arrived about the eleventh hour came forward,
Then when the first ones also came forward,
they considered that they would receive more.
arbitrati sunt quod plus essent accepturi:
And upon receiving it, they murmured against the father of the family,
‘These last have worked for one hour,
and you have made them equal to us,
But responding to one of them,
Did you not agree with me to one denarius?
Take what is yours and go.
But it is my will to give to this last,
volo autem et huic novissimo dare sicut et tibi.
Aut non licet mihi quod volo, facere?
And is it not lawful for me to do what I will?
an oculus tuus nequam est, quia ego bonus sum?
Or is your eye wicked because I am good?’
So then, the last shall be first,
et primi novissimi. Multi enim sunt vocati,
and the first shall be last. For many are called,
took the twelve disciples aside in private and said to them:
et Filius hominis tradetur principibus sacerdotum,
and the Son of man shall be handed over to the leaders of the priests and to the scribes.
And they shall condemn him to death.
et tradent eum gentibus ad illudendum, et flagellandum,
And they shall hand him over to the Gentiles to be mocked and scourged and crucified.
Tunc accessit ad eum mater filiorum Zebedæi cum filiis suis,
Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee approached him, with her sons, adoring him,
adorans et petens aliquid ab eo.
Dic ut sedeant hi duo filii mei,
She said to him, “Declare that these, my two sons,
may sit, one at your right hand,
et unus ad sinistram in regno tuo.
and the other at your left, in your kingdom.”
“You do not know what you are asking.
Potestis bibere calicem, quem ego bibiturus sum?
Are you able to drink from the chalice, from which I will drink?”
“From my chalice, indeed, you shall drink.
sedere autem ad dexteram meam vel sinistram non est meum dare vobis, sed quibus paratum est a Patre meo.
But to sit at my right or my left is not mine to give to you, but it is for those for whom it has been prepared by my Father.”
And the ten, upon hearing this,
became indignant with the two brothers.
Jesus autem vocavit eos ad se,
But Jesus called them to himself and said:
et ait: Scitis quia principes gentium dominantur eorum:
“You know that the first ones among the Gentiles are their rulers,
et qui majores sunt, potestatem exercent in eos.
and that those who are greater exercise power among them.
It shall not be this way among you.
sed quicumque voluerit inter vos major fieri,
But whoever will want to be greater among you,
et qui voluerit inter vos primus esse,
And whoever will want to be first among you,
Sicut Filius hominis non venit ministrari,
even as the Son of man has not come to be served,
et dare animam suam redemptionem pro multis.
and to give his life as a redemption for many.”
And as they were departing from Jericho,
et ecce duo cæci sedentes secus viam audierunt quia Jesus transiret:
And behold, two blind men, sitting by the way,
heard that Jesus was passing by; and they cried out,
Turba autem increpabat eos ut tacerent.
But the crowd rebuked them to be quiet.
But they cried out all the more,
and he called them and said,
that I might do for you?”
